overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing jurisdictional matters at an August 2014 workshop attended by a quorum outside a noticed meeting, though the violation was not intentional; a separate allegation of a private berating meeting was unsubstantiated.

allegations.summary: Committee members attended an August 2014 workshop with the superintendent, allegedly deliberating on district matters outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: While the question is a close one, we find that some of the matters discussed during the conversation between the Superintendent and the Committee are within the Committee's jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that after the workshop the superintendent privately berated committee members, a further meeting outside the open meeting law process.
allegations.key_passage: This complaint has provided no evidence to substantiate these claims, and the Committee denies that any such encounter occurred.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
